seoDescription: Learn how to operate a mini sewing machine with this step-by-step tutorial. This guide covers everything from initial setup to essential techniques, including how to wind a bobbin, properly thread the upper machine and lower bobbin, and get your machine ready to sew. Discover key tips for starting a seam, securing stitches without a reverse function, and finishing your work cleanly. This video provides the fundamental skills you need to get started with your portable sewing machine for beginner projects.

chapters.title: Getting Started & Unthreading the Machine
chapters.description: This chapter provides an introduction and shows how to prepare the mini sewing machine by removing the pre-loaded fabric and unthreading it.

chapters.title: Powering On & Preparing the Bobbin Winder
chapters.description: Learn how to connect the power supply and foot pedal, and how to activate the bobbin winding pin on the hand wheel.

chapters.title: How to Wind the Bobbin
chapters.description: Follow the step-by-step process for threading an empty bobbin, placing it on the winder, and using the foot pedal to wind the thread evenly.

chapters.title: Threading the Upper Machine: Spool and Tension Disks
chapters.description: This chapter covers setting up the thread from a bobbin spool and correctly guiding it through the first thread guide and into the tension disks.

chapters.title: Threading the Upper Machine: Take-Up Lever and Needle
chapters.description: Continue threading the machine by passing the thread through the take-up lever, the lower guides, and finally through the eye of the needle.

chapters.title: Loading the Lower Bobbin
chapters.description: Learn the correct way to insert the wound bobbin into the machine and use the hand wheel to bring the bottom thread up.

chapters.title: Tip: How to Start a Seam
chapters.description: Discover a crucial tip for starting your seam by manually using the hand wheel to prevent the thread from pulling out of the needle.

chapters.title: Technique: Securing Stitches Without Reverse
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to lock your stitches at the beginning and end of a seam by pivoting the fabric, since the machine has no reverse function.

chapters.title: Finishing a Seam & Final Tips
chapters.description: Learn the proper way to finish sewing, including a technique to release thread tension before cutting to avoid breakage.

summary:
## Getting Started
To begin, power up the machine using either the battery compartment or the power plug. The **foot pedal** must also be plugged in, unless you plan to use the on/off switch.

Use the **presser foot lever** at the back of the machine to lift the presser foot and place or remove fabric.

## Winding the Bobbin
1.  Pull up the **spool pin** and place your spool of thread on it.
2.  On the **hand wheel**, press the bobbin winder button in and turn it towards you to release the **bobbin winding pin**.
3.  Thread the end of the thread through a hole on your empty bobbin and push it firmly onto the winding pin.
4.  Hold the thread tail to create tension and use the foot pedal to wind the bobbin, moving the thread side-to-side for an even fill.
5.  Once full, cut the thread and push the winding pin back into the hand wheel, turning it away from you to lock it.

## Threading the Machine

### Upper Thread Path
Follow this specific path to thread the top part of the machine:
*   Place a wound bobbin on the thread holder pin or use the main spool pin.
*   Pass the thread from right to left through the **first thread guide**.
*   Pull the thread down firmly between the **tension disks**.
*   Guide the thread right to left through the **next guide**, then up.
*   Thread the **take-up lever** from right to left.
*   Pass the thread down through the **guide above the needle**.
*   Thread it through the last guide on the **needle bar**.
*   Finally, thread the **needle** from left to right. A needle threader can make this step easier.

### Loading the Lower Bobbin
1. Ensure your bobbin thread runs in a **clockwise direction**; it should look like the letter 'q' when held up.
2. Drop the bobbin into the bobbin holder.
3. Hold the top thread loosely and turn the **hand wheel** towards you one full rotation. This will loop the top thread around the bobbin thread.
4. Gently pull the top thread to bring the bobbin thread loop up. 
5. Pull both thread tails under the presser foot and towards the back.

## Essential Sewing Techniques

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Starting a Seam:** Before using the foot pedal, manually turn the **hand wheel** towards you a few times. This creates the first few stitches and prevents the thread from being pulled out of the needle when you start sewing.

> [!NOTE]
> **Securing Stitches (Backstitch):** This machine has no reverse function. To lock your stitches, sew a few stitches, stop with the needle down in the fabric, lift the presser foot, pivot the fabric 180°, sew a few stitches in reverse, then pivot back to continue your seam.

> [!TIP]
> **Finishing a Seam:** After your last stitch, keep the presser foot down and tap the foot pedal to run the machine for a moment. This pulls some slack thread through the mechanism, preventing thread breakage when you lift the presser foot and cut the threads.

What I'm going to show you today is how to thread the machine, how to wind the bobbin, and how to get it all set up. We're ready, if some thread does run out or if some thread comes out of the needle, you know exactly what to do. 

Okay, so what I'm going to do is I'm going to remove this fabric. So the presser foot is down at the moment, so I'm going to lift the presser foot. There's a little lever at the back here. I'm going to lift that up, and that will bring your presser foot up. I'm going to take that fabric out and I'm going to unthread the whole machine.

Now I'm going to plug the machine in so we have some power. So you can either insert your batteries at this stage or your power plug, and you'll also need your foot pedal plugged in, unless you want to use the on/off button there. 

So this is all plugged in and ready to go. Next you'll need your thread and your empty bobbin. So to wind the bobbin I'm going to pull this spool pin up here to put my thread onto, like so. And then I need to release this bobbin winding pin. So it's on the hand wheel here, looks like a little button. So I'm going to press it inwards and then turn my finger towards me and it should pop that little bobbin pin out. And to put it back in you just push it in and turn it away from you. Okay.

## How to Wind the Bobbin

And then I'm going to put the end of this thread through one of the holes and you can wind it on a bit if you like to get it started. And firmly push it on as you don't want it falling off while you're winding. Okay, so I'm going to put my foot on the presser foot... on the foot pedal, sorry. To take it off, pull it off gently. Okay, and you can use your little thread cutter on the side of the sewing machine there if you like. And then don't forget to push your pin back in. ## Threading the Upper Machine: Spool and Tension Disks

Now I'm going to thread the top part of the machine. So you can actually, if you want, just use this thread from the thread spool and thread it from here. Alright, we're going to thread the machine now. So this is your first thread guide, so you need to pass it through from right to left. Just going to pull it so I have a bit of thread to work with. Alright, next the thread needs to go into the tension disks, which are right here. So pull it down so it's sitting nicely in between those tension disks. The next thread guide is right here. You need to thread it through from right to left if you can get your fingers in there. Just make sure it doesn't get caught on anything. Okay.

## Threading the Upper Machine: Take-Up Lever and Needle

Your next thread guide is on the take-up lever up here, so you need to pass it through from right to left. Okay, and the next thread guide is right here. Now there is a light on here as well. Now I struggle with that, so I'm going to use this needle threader. So I'm going to put the needle threader in from the right, pull my thread through the threader and then pull it through there. ## Loading the Lower Bobbin

Next I'm going to load in the bobbin for the bottom thread. So to do this you need to have your bobbin, your thread running in a clockwise direction. So when you hold your bobbin up with your thread, it should almost look like the letter q. So that'll help you remember.

And then once the needle comes back up, you can gently pull the thread towards you and that should bring the bobbin thread up as well. And then you can carefully just pull it out, put your threads under the presser foot there and towards the back and your machine is ready to sew. Just replace that bobbin cover there. There we go.

## Tip: How to Start a Seam

Okay, so before you start sewing with your mini sewing machine, I'm going to sew a bit of fabric and share a few tips that I've worked out that'll help with using the sewing machine. So I've got my fabric ready, my machine is all threaded up. 

What I recommend you do is put your fabric under the presser foot, lower your presser foot down, and before you put your foot on the foot pedal, turn the hand wheel towards you a couple of times, just to put that needle up and down and put a couple of stitches into the fabric. And that'll hold your thread in, because I found if I didn't do that, the machine will want to pull the thread out and it would break and I'd have to rethread the machine.

## Technique: Securing Stitches Without Reverse

Okay, so that should be good to go. ## Finishing a Seam & Final Tips

Okay, and the same again when you get to the end. Put your needle in the down position, secure your stitching.
